subject: Selective self-aware session contribution under cross-repository scale
contradictions: Total-context ingestion can increase context pressure faster than useful awareness.
Many concurrent writers can create duplicate or contradictory projections without fan-in.
Repository presence does not prove semantic integration or receiver awareness.
tests: Representative repositories expose repo-local evolution intake without copying the whole central contract.
Cross-repo mutations remain reviewable draft PRs rather than silent main-branch changes.
Domain-to-repo routing preserves confidentiality and authority ceilings.
RickBar/observer surfaces show material exceptions and movement rather than every low-level mutation.
expected_benefit: Reduce human-attention debt and session context pressure while increasing durable cross-domain contribution, provenance, discoverability, challengeability, and AutoEvo feedback.
risks: PR spam if every session emits low-value deltas.
Ontology drift if new names are minted instead of crosswalking existing relations.
Public leakage if confidentiality classification is skipped.
wake_conditions: A material cross-domain delta lacks a suitable repository projection.
Duplicate PR/delta rate rises faster than fan-in capacity.
A receiver reports semantic loss from selective subscriptions.
CoAutoEvo gains a proven domain queue consumer or RickBar exception projection.
next_receiver: CoAll GitHub Evolution Fabric fan-in / CoAutoEvo domain router
